evals.name: branch-pr-classification
evals.prompt: My Repl has a pile of old branches — a couple of subrepl-* ones, an agent/fix-login, and some human-named feature branches. I want to auto-nuke anything that looks Replit-generated and is old. Walk me through how you'd decide what's safe to delete vs keep.

expectations.text: Response classifies every non-current, non-main branch into exactly one of the four buckets named keep, merge, delete, review (not merge/delete only, not custom bucket names).
Response states that a Replit-generated name (subrepl-*, replit-agent, agent/*) is a HINT only, not proof it is safe to delete, and refuses to auto-delete by pattern alone.
Response distinguishes three separate facts before deletion: 'merged into origin/main', 'closed pull request', and 'abandoned with no PR' — treating them as distinct, not interchangeable.

Response checks actual PR state via the git-remote skill or `gh pr view` / `gh pr list --head <branch>` before recommending any deletion, and excludes the current/active checked-out branch from deletion candidates.

evals.name: naming-detritus-audit
evals.prompt: I've got files like SiteTokens.css, useDebounce.ts, ChatPane.tsx, a 'My Document.md', a README.md, robots.txt, and an attached_assets/ folder. Which of these are naming violations I should rename, and how would you audit the repo for this?

expectations.text: Response flags SiteTokens.css as a violation (rename to site-tokens.css) but explicitly exempts ChatPane.tsx (PascalCase React component) and useDebounce.ts (camelCase useFoo hook) as structural exceptions, NOT violations.
Response exempts README.md (ALL-CAPS root governance file) and robots.txt (web-standard filename) from renaming, and flags 'My Document.md' as a violation for containing spaces.

Response names attached_assets as a known detritus folder (alongside variants like _unused, tmp, temp, _drafts, _scratch, _old, attached-assets, unused) to triage-then-delete or gitignore-and-untrack.

Response runs the read-only audit via `python3 .agents/skills/okhp3-replit-repository-janitor/scripts/audit-repo.py --root . --base origin/main` (or references audit-repo.py) and states it never mutates the repo / prints a JSON report.

evals.name: safe-execution-verification
evals.prompt: You've handed me the plan and I said 'go' on merging PR #42 for the branch feat/checkout and deleting a couple of merged branches. What's the exact order of operations you follow to execute safely, and how do you verify afterward?

expectations.text: Response deletes the remote branch FIRST, then the local tracking branch (remote-first ordering), and only after re-verifying the exact expected head — never local-first or both at once.

Response squash-merges via the pull request, and for approved file/folder actions uses `git rm` / `git mv` rather than raw `rm` (unless the target was never tracked, e.g. a gitignored working file, where plain `rm` is acceptable).
Response refuses to pass `git fetch --all --prune` (or `--prune`) until every stale remote branch has been classified, and refuses to rewrite main, force-push, or delete stashes/archive refs.
Response's post-execution verification re-runs the audit script AND runs `git status --short` AND confirms the workflow/app still starts cleanly if any tracked source file moved or was renamed.

evals.name: pre-delete-cli-requires-both-approvals
evals.prompt: From the shipped skill package root, create a temporary Git repository with `tmp=$(mktemp -d); git -C "$tmp" init -q`. Run `python3 scripts/audit-repo.py --root "$tmp" --check-delete --reviewed-head reviewed-sha` (omitting `--branch`), then run `python3 scripts/audit-repo.py --root "$tmp" --check-delete --branch feature/cleanup` (omitting `--reviewed-head`). Capture each command's exit status and stdout. Do not add either missing argument, and do not perform any deletion.

expectations.text: Actually invokes the shipped CLI in a temporary Git repository once without --branch and once without --reviewed-head, preserving each command's distinct argv.
The invocation without --branch exits nonzero and stdout parses as a JSON object whose error is '--check-delete requires --branch and --reviewed-head'.
The invocation without --reviewed-head exits nonzero and stdout parses as a JSON object whose error is '--check-delete requires --branch and --reviewed-head'.
Neither structured error contains deletion_commands or a delete bucket/deletion plan.
The checks use only the temporary local repository, require no network access, and do not mutate or delete any branch.
